title: Labneh
description: Labneh is a traditional Arabic strained yogurt cheese known for its thick, creamy texture and tangy flavor. Made by draining Greek yogurt, it is commonly served as a dip, spread, or part of a mezze platter with olive oil, herbs, and spices.

ingredients.title: Ingredients (Yield: ~500g Labneh)
items: Olive oil (extra virgin) – for serving, ~3–4 tbsp
Za’atar spice blend – 1–2 tsp, optional garnish
Fresh herbs (mint, thyme, or parsley) – finely chopped, optional garnish

ingredients.title: Equipment
items: Cheesecloth or a fine muslin cloth

instruction.title: Instructions
steps:
1. Prep Yogurt:
• In a mixing bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt until smooth.
• Stir in the salt evenly.

2. Drain Yogurt:
• Line a colander with cheesecloth and place over a bowl.
• Pour the yogurt into the cheesecloth. Fold over the edges to cover.
• Place in the refrigerator to drain for 24–48 hours depending on desired thickness.
• 24 hours: creamy, spreadable labneh.
• 48 hours: thicker, cream cheese-like texture.

3. Check Consistency:
• After draining, gently press to remove excess whey.
• Transfer to a serving dish.

4. Presentation:
• Make a small well in the center.
• Drizzle extra virgin olive oil generously.
• Top with za’atar, toasted pine nuts, or fresh herbs.

5. Storage:
• Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
• Keep a thin layer of olive oil on top to preserve freshness.

servingSuggestions.title: This labneh is perfect as:
items: Mezze platter (with olives, vegetables, and fresh bread)

chefTips: Use high-quality full-fat Greek yogurt for the best creamy texture.
Do not skip refrigeration during draining for safe fermentation and texture development.
Longer draining time creates thicker, cream cheese-like labneh.
For restaurant-style presentation, swirl labneh on a plate and drizzle olive oil with herbs and spices.
